CRM.rationale: Salesforce presents a solid fundamental picture with improving profitability and a dominant market position, combined with a meaningful valuation discount versus its own recent history. The company shows accelerating revenue growth (QoQ revenue +4.1%, EPS +23.3% from Q1 to Q2 FY26), strong gross margins (~78%), and expanding operating margins. The balance sheet is healthy with low leverage (debt-to-equity 0.14) and substantial equity ($61.3B). Agentforce and Data Cloud are growing at triple-digit rates (~$1.4B combined ARR, up 114% YoY), providing a credible AI-driven growth vector. On valuation, the P/E has compressed from ~56x a year ago to ~37x currently — a 34% multiple contraction — while earnings are growing, making the stock meaningfully cheaper versus its own history. The P/B of 2.9x is near the bottom of its 2.7-4.8 range. However, several factors temper conviction: (1) operating cash flow was volatile and weak in the latest quarter ($740M vs $6.48B prior), (2) AI disruption fears remain a genuine overhang on the SaaS model, (3) the stock has declined ~35% YTD suggesting the market is pricing in real risks, and (4) there is no clear near-term dated catalyst beyond the upcoming Q1 FY27 earnings where consensus expects EPS of $2.30 (+18.6% YoY).
